Thanks — I pulled the pcap and a quick look shows repeated CRLF-only delimiter appearances mid-stream and several truncated chunk frames. Symptoms line up with the streaming parser dropping a delimiter and failing to re-sync, which would cause the runtime to timeout and return 502.

Customer is using client-sdk 1.4.2 (we ship streaming framing change in 1.5.0). Hypothesis: older SDK emits a trailing delimiter pattern we recently hardened against in the runtime; under high throughput it surfaces as a parser state machine mismatch.

Asks:
- Aditya: can you confirm whether any runtime-side parser configs changed in the last deploy?
- Rishi: flag as potential regression for SDK/runtime contract; we may need an emergency compatibility doc and a temporary routing policy to fallback to non-streaming endpoints for StorCommerce.

I'll attach a short trace and some annotated pcap excerpts.

Ben

Ben — no parser config changes in the last 72 hours on dedicated pools serving StorCommerce. I spun up a repro using their pcap and the runtime log shows repeated "DELIM_RESYNC" warnings followed by a 3s stall and the request dying with an upstream parse error.

Immediate mitigations I can push:
- Apply a tolerant resync patch (drops at most one misplaced delimiter) to the stream parser on the staging routing group and promote to a control plane rule to route StorCommerce traffic there.
- Add a temporary policy that routes StorCommerce to the legacy non-streaming path (adds ~60ms p50 but avoids stalls).

Markus — we should decide whether to opt for a fast routing fallback or to ship the parser patch to production. Patch is low-risk but needs coordinated rollout and monitoring.
